skill.name: pitfalls-blockchain
skill.description: Guides safe blockchain RPC usage, gas estimation, multicall handling, nonce management, and multi-chain configuration for smart contract integrations.
skill.summary: Avoid common blockchain integration mistakes in RPC calls, gas handling, retries, and transaction management.
skill.author: BarisSozen

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, TypeScript template literals, example RPC URLs, and illustrative environment variable references. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, wallet access, or executable command behavior was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Example provider URLs include placeholder API key paths.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that users must supply their own RPC endpoints and should avoid committing real provider keys.

remediation.issue: Environment variable examples may be mistaken for secret access by automated scanners.
remediation.suggestion: State that RPC URL variables are read only by user applications, not by the skill itself.

content.value_statement: Blockchain integrations often fail through weak RPC handling, bad gas assumptions, or unsafe transaction flow. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused review guidance for safer smart contract interactions.
actual_capabilities: Reviews contract call error handling for try/catch coverage and graceful revert handling.
Checks gas estimation patterns, buffer usage, EIP-1559 fee fields, and simulation before execution.
Evaluates multicall usage for individual failure handling with allowFailure enabled.
Guides chain-specific RPC configuration, confirmations, block times, and native token settings.
Highlights nonce management patterns for concurrent transaction submission.
Suggests retry and fallback RPC patterns for rate limits and provider outages.
limitations: Does not verify live chain state, token liquidity, or RPC provider availability.
Does not audit smart contract bytecode or prove transaction profitability.
Does not replace wallet security review or private key handling controls.
Examples require adaptation to the user's blockchain library and chain targets.

use_cases.title: Review dApp Transaction Code
use_cases.description: Find missing gas estimates, confirmation waits, simulations, and revert handling before a user-facing release.

use_cases.title: Harden Multi-Chain Integrations
use_cases.description: Check that each supported chain has appropriate RPC settings, confirmations, block timing, and fallback behavior.

use_cases.title: Debug Unreliable RPC Workflows
use_cases.description: Use the checklist to diagnose quote failures, rate limits, nonce conflicts, and inconsistent multicall results.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Contract Calls
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small Web3 function.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the pitfalls-blockchain checklist to review this contract call flow. Focus on error handling, address validation, and graceful handling of reverted calls.

prompt_templates.title: Review Gas and Simulation Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this transaction code for gas estimation, EIP-1559 fee usage, gas buffers, and call simulation before sending the transaction.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Multi-Chain Configuration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced configuration review across several networks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this multi-chain configuration for RPC endpoint handling, confirmation counts, block time assumptions, native token settings, and safe fallback behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Production Transaction Reliability
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced reliability review for production services.
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a blockchain reliability review of this transaction pipeline. Include nonce management, retry policy, rate limits, multicall behavior, confirmations, and likely failure modes.

output_examples.input: Review a swap function that sends a transaction without estimating gas or simulating first.
output: The flow should estimate gas before sending and add a bounded buffer.
The transaction should be simulated before execution to catch likely reverts.
The caller should wait for the required confirmations before treating the swap as final.

output_examples.input: Check a multicall quote workflow that stops when one pool reverts.
output: Use individual failure handling so one missing pool does not break the full quote batch.
Log failed token pairs at a safe level and continue processing the successful results.
Return null or a typed unavailable result for low-liquidity pairs.

output_examples.input: Review RPC settings for Ethereum and Polygon support.
output: Confirm each chain has its own RPC URL, confirmation count, block time, and native token metadata.
Use fallback endpoints and retry with backoff for rate limits.
Avoid committing real provider keys in configuration or examples.

best_practices: Simulate transactions and estimate gas before sending any state-changing contract call.
Handle expected blockchain failures as normal outcomes, including reverts, missing pools, and rate limits.
Use chain-specific confirmation counts, nonce tracking, and RPC fallback policies.
anti_patterns: Assuming a successful RPC response means a transaction is finalized.
Letting one reverted multicall item fail an entire batch of independent reads.
Using one gas, confirmation, or block-time assumption for every supported chain.

faq.question: Does this skill send blockchain transactions?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and examples for safer transaction code.

faq.question: Can it verify whether a contract is safe?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on integration pitfalls, not full smart contract security auditing.

faq.question: Does it require access to private keys?
faq.answer: No. The skill should not need wallet keys, seed phrases, or signing credentials.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it useful for multi-chain applications?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes checks for chain-specific RPC URLs, confirmations, block times, and native tokens.

faq.question: Can it replace live testing on a fork or testnet?
faq.answer: No. Use it for review guidance, then validate behavior in a realistic test environment.
